text.p: These are significant stories in the Nigerian press on Tuesday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.

- Strong indications emerge that a fresh voter register will be prepared across Nigeria for the conduct of forthcoming local government elections, the next step on the military government's timetable to restore civilian rule.
- The problems of clearing cargo from ports have been further complicated by conflicting interpretations of government directives.
- A decree that will compel government agencies to submit information promptly to the Federal Office of Statistics is being prepared, the Daily Times learns.

- Ten heavy oil and bitumen wells have been found in southwestern Nigeria during explorations by a Canadian company. The company is believed to have designed a plan to exploit the resources for local consumption.
- The ban on the importation of gypsum is a serious threat to Nigeria's cement industry, the chairman of Benue Cement Company says.

- Intercellular Nigeria Limited is on Thursday to sign a $6 million contract for mobile telephones with America's Motorola. The contract is the first phase of a 1.0 billion naira project which will be able to supply 10,000 subsrcibers in Lagos and Abuja by the first quarter of next year.

- A World Bank team has concluded plans to send a poverty allieviation team to Nigeria early next year. The team will work with the relevant sub-committee of "Vision 2010", the economic plan which is being prepared for the next century.
